messages:
maya: hey team — CI linkcheck started failing on main after the mkdocs migration. lots of broken fragment warnings, odd ones point to headings that look fine locally. anyone else seeing this?
jon: yeah saw it earlier. build log shows fragments like '#usage ' (note trailing space) and some non-breaking space characters.
maya: exact error excerpt from CI:
```
WARNING -  broken fragment: /docs/guides/usage.md: '#usage '
```
alex: mm. local `mkdocs serve` is forgiving but the CI linkcheck enforces exact fragment matches. slugify/anchor generation must differ between the old pipeline and mkdocs' slugger.
jon: looks like some headings have trailing whitespace or invisible unicode (NBSP, ZWNJ) that mkdocs turns into different anchors. linkcheck complains because the generated anchor doesn't match the link target.
priya: simple fix: sanitize headings during build (trim trailing whitespace, normalize unicode spaces) or add a small pre-build hook to normalize IDs. less risky than mass-editing source files.
alex: I made a tiny plugin a while back for heading cleanup — can drop it as a quick patch. it runs before slug generation and trims/normalizes headings.
docs-bot: ci/linkcheck job failed on main — 8 broken fragments. see run https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/7890
jon: can you paste one offending heading (raw) so we can reproduce?
maya: pasted the markdown snippet:
```markdown
## Usage  
Some description...
```
jon: there — NBSP after the heading text. mkdocs slugify will include or drop it differently than previous tooling.
alex: PR plan: add a small mkdocs plugin and an entry in mkdocs.yml enabling it. plugin will: strip trailing whitespace, normalize NBSP/ZWJ to plain spaces, collapse repeated spaces, and ensure heading IDs match slugify behavior.
maya: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4567 — contains plugin + mkdocs.yml change + a note in the migration guide. local `mkdocs build` + `mkdocs link-check` clean for me.
priya: LGTM after a tiny changelog entry and a line in the migration guide explaining that some heading IDs may change and how to pin them with explicit IDs.
alex: pushed a compact plugin snippet to the PR. snippet:
```python
import re
from mkdocs.plugins import BasePlugin
class HeadingSanitizer(BasePlugin):
    def on_page_markdown(self, markdown, page, config, files):
        # trim trailing whitespace and normalize non-breaking spaces in headings
        def fix_heading(m):
            text = m.group(1).rstrip()
            text = text.replace(' ', ' ').replace('​', '')
            return text + '\n'
        return re.sub(r'(^#+\s.*$)(?:\n)?', fix_heading, markdown, flags=re.M)
```
jon: nice. can you add a unit test that covers headings with trailing space, NBSP, and zero-width chars? prevents regressions.
maya: will add tests. @docs-bot could you re-run linkcheck for PR-4567 once tests land?
docs-bot: linkcheck re-run queued for PR-4567 — build 7901 :hourglass_flowing_sand:
deploy-bot: build 7901 finished — linkcheck: 0 warnings :tada:
maya: :tada: awesome. thanks everyone — i'll merge after changelog line and a short note in the migration guide about Docusaurus vs MkDocs slug differences.
alex: FYI: Docusaurus slugger behaves slightly differently for some unicode sequences; we should call that out in the migration doc so external links don't break.
priya: I'll add a short section under docs/migration.md explaining the difference and how to provide explicit IDs if you rely on the old behavior.
jon: after merge let's run a quick site sanity sweep (search for `#` fragment links) and send a small redirect PR if we find high-traffic pages with changed anchors.
maya: agreed. will open a follow-up if we see analytics hits. thanks again!
